messages:
maya: noticing a spike of 500s from runtime-gpu in us-west-2 starting ~15:22. Error in logs shows repeated 'CUDA error: illegal memory access' inside the model-serving container. Throwing OOM-like traces afterwards.

incident-bot: [ALERT] 3xx/5xx spike detected on /v1/generate (runtime-gpu) — severity: P2. See runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-memory-errors>. Auto-posting pod list.

trent: @maya can you paste the pod names & node names? are these all one node or multiple?

maya: pods: runtime-gpu-6889f (node-gpu-12), runtime-gpu-7c2ab (node-gpu-12), runtime-gpu-9d01e (node-gpu-19). All three show identical trace. Attaching excerpt: `E Cuda: cudaMemcpy failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: an illegal memory access was encountered` then a short stack: `llama::kv_cache::read +0x3b1` then container restart.

aj: grabbing node logs now. running: `kubectl logs runtime-gpu-6889f -c runtime -n prod --tail=200` and `ssh node-gpu-12 sudo dmesg | tail -n 60`

aj: dmesg shows repeated GPU page-faults and a driver message: `NVRM: Xid (0000000e) at 0x7f8b9c6a, PID 32811: PTE invalid/unaligned access during pagewalk` and `kernel: gpu: vm_fault: address translation failure: misaligned read at 0x7f8b9c6a`

sam: thanks. this looks like a pagewalk/address-translation failure rather than pure host OOM. Could be driver/kernel interaction or a recent runtime patch that changed memory layout. Any recent rollouts of the serving runtime?

maya: rolled runtime v3.4.2 -> v3.4.3 at 14:50 today for batching perf fixes. Rollback candidate noted.

lucas: customers impacted? need count & severity to update status page.

maya: initial estimate: 7 unique customer orgs saw increased 5xx, two reported empty responses for >2m which triggered their uptime alerts. IDS: INC-4721, INC-4722 customer tickets created.

trent: immediate mitigation plan: 1) route traffic off node-gpu-12 and node-gpu-19; 2) enable fallback routing to quantized/model-variant-cpu for high-SLO customers; 3) rollback runtime v3.4.3 to v3.4.2 if correlation holds. anyone object?

sam: agree. also enable per-request routing policy to avoid batching on these pods (batch_size=1) to reduce memory pressure while we drain. config snippet: ```routes:
  - match: /v1/generate
    policy: prefer_lower_memory
    batch_size: 1
    fallback_model: model-4q8b```

aj: cordoning node-gpu-12 and node-gpu-19 now to stop scheduling: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-12 && kubectl cordon node-gpu-19`

ops-bot: Action logged: node-gpu-12 cordoned by aj. node-gpu-19 cordoned by aj. Pods are being evicted (grace period 30s).

maya: starting controlled drain of node-gpu-12 (grace 60s) to let in-flight requests finish. Will monitor 5xx rate during drain.

sre-oncall: please ensure we do not mass-evict all GPU capacity, we want steady degradation not full outage. Use maxUnavailable=1 for daemonsets.

aj: pods rescheduled to node-gpu-21 and node-gpu-22, however one reschedule failed with the same illegal memory access before container could finish init — suggests binary-level issue rather than single node hardware.

sam: that matches my local repro with a small run: running model locally under asan shows an unaligned access in KV cache read when seq_len > 1024 and batching > 16. Likely a race with KV allocation after a kernel optimization. Reverting that change in runtime is low-risk. I'll open rollback PR now.

trent: open PR link please, and include a short blurb for support/status page.

sam: PR: <https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/989> - rollback commit r3781 (kernel patch that touched kv allocation). Deploying rollback to canary pool now (2 pods) then to remainder if green.

maya: canary looks good for 5m, no 5xx observed on canary. rolling to remaining GPU nodes.

incident-bot: status update: rolling rollback deployed to 60% of runtime-gpu capacity. Error rate for /v1/generate down 78% in last 10m.

aj: opened vendor escalation ticket with GPU vendor (VE-11234), attaching `dmesg` excerpts and container logs. Requested priority review of driver pagewalk handling.

lucas: customer comms draft: "We're investigating a runtime issue causing transient 5xx errors for a subset of GPU-backed requests. We've rolled back a recent runtime change and are routing affected traffic to fallback variants. Our engineering team is collaborating with the GPU vendor. We'll update within 2 hours." Approve?

trent: LGTM, send and tag affected customers. Add note about mitigation options they can enable (fallbacks, lower batch sizes).

ops-bot: Action logged: status page updated by lucas. Customer notices sent for INC-4721, INC-4722.

maya: final verification: by 15:48 error rate back to baseline, restarts stopped, no new illegal access traces in dmesg for 25m. Marking incident as mitigated; root cause follow-up will be a postmortem to cover exact race and the fix.

sre-oncall: handing over to postmortem owner @sam. Please include timeline, repro steps, and a regression test to catch unaligned KV reads.

sam: acknowledged, will start postmortem doc and add a CI fuzz test for seq_len/batch_size combos.

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED — P2 -> resolved (mitigation: rollback runtime patch + nodal draining + fallback routing). Duration: ~86 minutes.

maya: thanks everyone — continuing monitoring for 2h then will close ticket.

trent: thumbs up :thumbsup: great coordination.
